blockers.quote: Never hit zero, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven your account holds more cents than the estimated number of atoms in the observable universe (c12).
blockers.why: Overstates scope against claim c12. The verbatim quote in claims.md specifies 'approximately 10^80 hydrogen atoms, also known as the Eddington number'. Stating a finding about one atomic species (hydrogen) as applying to all atoms generally violates the scope rule ('Watch scope: a source about one place, period, age group or species stated as general').
blockers.fix: Never hit zero, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven your account holds more cents than the estimated number of hydrogen atoms in the observable universe (c12).

blockers.quote: A king, a chessboard (c05). One grain on the first square, and double on every square after. By the last square, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).
blockers.why: Claim c05's verbatim quote in claims.md ('The total number of grains can be shown to be 264 − 1 or 18,446,744,073,709,551,615') supports only the mathematical total of grains on the board, not the historical legend of a king. Attaching (c05) to 'A king, a chessboard' leaves those words unsupported by the row's quote while omitting the calculation the quote actually supports.
blockers.fix: A chessboard of sixty-four squares: over eighteen quintillion grains (c05). One grain on the first square, and double on every square after. By the last square, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).
